title: Silver chloride in salty water
hook: A silver salt dissolves a little in pure water. Does salty water change how much?

knows: that salts dissolve only up to a limit
that dissolved salts are separate ions
doesNotKnow: that adding an ion already present lowers how much of the other ion can stay dissolved
that the two ions' concentrations multiply to a fixed ceiling

misconception: A salt's solubility is a fixed number of grams per litre, whatever else is in the water.
objective: The learner can say that in 0.10 mol/L chloride the silver ion concentration over AgCl crystals falls from about 1.3 × 10⁻⁵ to about 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ mol/L, because the product of the two ion concentrations has a fixed ceiling of about 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰.

claims.text: Silver chloride (AgCl) is a salt that dissolves only a little in water, giving silver ions (Ag⁺) and chloride ions (Cl⁻).
claims.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, solubility product constants; AgCl is sparingly soluble.

claims.text: While AgCl crystals remain in the water, [Ag⁺] × [Cl⁻] equals about 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ (mol/L)² at 25 °C.
claims.source: Ksp(AgCl) = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ at 25 °C (CRC Handbook). Concentrations used in place of activities, an approximation.

claims.text: In pure water [Ag⁺] is about 1.3 × 10⁻⁵ mol/L.
In water with 0.10 mol/L of NaCl, [Ag⁺] is about 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ mol/L, about 7,500 times lower than in pure water.
claims.source: [Ag⁺] = 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁰ / 0.10 = 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ mol/L (the solved quadratic gives the same to 2 figures); 1.34 × 10⁻⁵ / 1.8 × 10⁻⁹ = 7,450 (node; Demo.tsx RATIO). Ignores activity and soluble AgCl₂⁻ complexes, which matter more at higher chloride.

claims.text: The intermediate steps, 0.001 and 0.010 mol/L of NaCl, give [Ag⁺] of about 1.8 × 10⁻⁷ and 1.8 × 10⁻⁸ mol/L.
claims.source: 1.8e-10 / 0.001 = 1.8e-7; 1.8e-10 / 0.01 = 1.8e-8 (node; the exact quadratic differs by under 0.1%).

claims.text: Adding one of the ions already in the solution lowers how much of the other can stay dissolved (the common-ion effect).
claims.source: Atkins, Physical Chemistry / Chemical Principles, common-ion effect; Chemistry LibreTexts.

claims.text: Square brackets mean moles per litre: [Ag⁺] is the number of moles of silver ions in each litre.

recall.question: A sparingly soluble salt has an ion-product ceiling of 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ (mol/L)². If the water already holds 0.01 mol/L of the salt's negative ion, the positive ion's concentration over crystals is about…
recall.why: The ceiling divided by the existing ion's concentration: 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 0.01 = 1 × 10⁻⁸ mol/L.
